Name: recompute_loop_forgetting
Title: Recompute Loops: Overthinking as Retrieval Failure of the Model's Own Scratchpad
Short Hypothesis: A meaningful fraction of wasted reasoning tokens are spent re-deriving intermediate results the model already computed earlier in the same chain-of-thought. We define a 'recompute loop' operationally as a value-producing statement whose result is semantically equivalent to one already established earlier in the trace AND that re-derives rather than merely references it, excluding legitimate self-verification (re-derivation that changes or checks the earlier value) and paraphrased restatement (no new derivation). We hypothesize recompute loops arise because the model fails to retrieve its own prior conclusion from context - a working-memory/retrieval failure - detectable at the recomputation onset via degraded attention to the earlier result, and causally suppressible by injecting that result's representation. The primary contribution is the mechanistic characterization (recompute loops as retrieval failure); the onset-triggered memory-injection intervention is a secondary application.
Related Work: Existing efficiency work treats redundancy as scattered attention or verbosity: Think Clearly (2025) prunes low-attention tokens reactively; TTS (2025) labels steps decorative vs. load-bearing post-hoc; NLDD (2026) shows a reasoning horizon; When More is Less (2025) targets a global optimal length. Retrieval/reuse methods operate ACROSS problems or via external memory: Reuse-Don't-Recompute and Memory-of-Thought cache and re-inject solutions from PRIOR problems; Thought-Retriever retrieves from an external store. Working-memory interpretability (LLMs Do Not Have Human-Like Working Memory, 2025; Self-Attention Limits Working Memory Capacity, 2024; Strong Memory Weak Control, 2025) documents self-contradiction and drift but proposes no efficiency mechanism. The one-line deltas: Think Clearly/TTS remove tokens by attention/importance regardless of why they are redundant; Reuse-Don't-Recompute/Memory-of-Thought/Thought-Retriever reuse content across problems via external memory; we instead identify a specific WITHIN-TRACE redundancy - recomputation of an already-derived intermediate - and attribute it to a retrieval failure of the model's own scratchpad, intervening at onset with an internal memory injection. We narrow our novelty claim accordingly: not the first to identify redundancy, but the first to characterize within-trace recomputation as a retrieval-failure phenomenon and to intervene at its onset.
Abstract: Reasoning models 'overthink,' but the structure of the wasted computation is poorly understood. We identify a concrete pattern we call recompute loops: within a single chain of thought, the model re-derives an intermediate quantity (an equation, a partial sum, a constraint, a candidate answer) it already established earlier in the same trace, without checking or changing it. We hypothesize recompute loops are a symptom of the model failing to retrieve its own prior conclusion from context - a working-memory/retrieval failure - rather than generic verbosity, and we treat the mechanistic characterization as the primary contribution. First, we build an automatic detector for recomputed results by matching semantically-equivalent value-producing statements across a trace, with explicit exclusion rules for self-verification and paraphrase, and quantify their token cost across GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and GPQA on DeepSeek-R1 distills (1.5B-14B) and Qwen3. Second, we test the retrieval-failure hypothesis with a causal chain: at recomputation onset we measure attention back to the original derivation, probe whether the earlier result is still linearly recoverable, patch in that result's representation, and ablate the intervention timing. Third, we turn the diagnosis into a training-free onset-triggered memory injection that reminds the model of the already-derived result so it continues instead of re-deriving. We evaluate token savings at equal accuracy against reactive pruning, verbosity steering, and length-aware baselines, report the savings as tokens, wall-clock latency, and serving cost, and separate the user-facing benefit (faster, cheaper answers) from the research benefit (a named, quantifiable waste category linked to working-memory limits). We analyze failure cases where recomputation is corrective.
Experiments:
Compute fits an academic node (<= 8xA100-80GB). Primary model: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, frozen; only a cheap onset probe is trainable. Scale sweep: R1-Qwen distills 1.5B/7B/14B and Qwen3-8B. Decoding: temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, max 16k thinking tokens, seeds 0/1/2 on every reported number. CoT segmented into steps by newline/step delimiters. Datasets, used as released: GSM8K test (1319), MATH500 (500), AIME 2024+2025 (60), GPQA-Diamond (198). Operational labels (pre-registered): a value-producing statement is a RECOMPUTE if its computed value is semantically equivalent to an earlier statement's value AND it re-executes the derivation; it is EXCLUDED if it verifies/changes the earlier value (self-correction) or merely restates it without derivation (paraphrase). Positive example: earlier 'so x=12', later '3*4=12' re-derived in a fresh sub-derivation. Negative examples: 'let me double-check: 3*4=12, yes' (verification), 'recall x=12' (paraphrase). Annotation guidelines and these rules are fixed before scoring.

Experiment 1 (H1 - Recompute loops exist and are costly): Detector parses value-producing statements and flags recomputes via an LLM-judge under the operational rules. Detector validity: two annotators label a 300-statement sample against the guidelines; report precision/recall and inter-annotator agreement (kappa). Decisive metric: fraction of thinking tokens attributable to recompute loops per dataset. Convincing: recompute loops account for >= 15% of thinking tokens on average at detector precision >= 0.8 and annotator kappa > 0.6. Indecision: token fraction in [7%, 15%] or precision in [0.65, 0.8]. Negative (< 7% of tokens or precision < 0.65): not a material or reliably measurable source of waste.

Experiment 2 (H1 - Distinct from generic waste, verification, and paraphrase): Show recompute loops are a distinct category. Correlate recompute-token fraction with total tokens and with 'wasted tokens' (tokens after the last accuracy-changing step, truncate-and-resume); compute overlap with TTS decorative labels; and report the share of flagged events that survive the verification/paraphrase exclusion rules. Decisive metric: share of recompute tokens on steps labeled load-bearing (non-decorative). Convincing: > 40% of recompute tokens sit on non-decorative steps AND < 15% of initially-flagged events are reclassified as verification/paraphrase under audit. Indecision: 25-40% non-decorative. Negative (< 25% non-decorative): largely a subset of decorative waste.

Experiment 3 (H2 - Retrieval-failure signature): At each recompute onset measure attention mass to the tokens of the original derivation vs. matched control positions where the same result is referenced/reused without recomputation. Decisive metric: paired difference in attention-to-original (recompute onsets vs. reuse controls). Convincing: recompute onsets show significantly lower attention (p < 0.01, Cohen's d > 0.5), localized to few heads. Indecision: 0.2 < d < 0.5. Negative (d < 0.2): no degraded self-attention, refuting the retrieval-failure mechanism (an informative negative).

Experiment 4 (H2 - Causal chain: probe, patch, timing): Strengthen the causal argument in three linked tests. (a) Probing: at onset, test whether the earlier result is still linearly recoverable from the residual (recoverability should be degraded vs. reuse controls). (b) Patching: patch in the residual-stream representation of the original result and measure the drop in probability of continuing the recomputation, vs. a norm-matched random patch. (c) Timing ablation: apply the patch at onset, one step before, and one step after, to show the effect is specific to onset. Decisive metric: recompute-continuation probability drop under true patch vs. random patch, and its dependence on timing. Convincing: true-result patch reduces recompute-continuation by >= 20 points (vs. < 5 random), maximized at onset. Indecision: reduction in [8, 20] points. Negative (< 8 points): injecting the earlier result does not causally suppress recomputation.

Experiment 5 (H3 - Memory injection: savings, cost, and detector ablation): Run the detector online via a cheap residual-stream onset probe (trained on Experiment-1 labels, 40/60 split by problem); on predicted onset, inject a terse reminder of the prior result and continue. Ablation: also run (i) injection WITHOUT the mechanistic detector (inject at fixed intervals) and (ii) the detector WITHOUT injection (just flag), to isolate what each component contributes. Systems compared on all four datasets: memory injection vs. (a) no intervention, (b) fixed truncation matched to injection mean budget, (c) Think Clearly reactive pruning, (d) verbosity/CREST-style steering, (e) length-aware filtering. Decisive metric: token reduction at equal accuracy (percent reduction while accuracy within 1 point). Secondary: recompute-loop count reduction, mean tokens, wall-clock latency, and estimated serving-cost reduction per query. Convincing: >= 15% token reduction within 1 point on GSM8K and MATH500 with recompute count cut >= 50%, matching or beating every baseline on the frontier, and the detector-guided variant beating the fixed-interval variant. Indecision: reduction in [7%, 15%] or a frontier-tie - the diagnosis (Experiments 1-4) is then the standalone contribution. Negative (< 7% or > 1 point loss): no usable savings.

Experiment 6 (H3 - Preserving corrective re-derivation, null-friendly analysis): Label a sample of onsets as corrective vs. blind, measure accuracy impact of suppressing each class, and additionally characterize WHEN recomputation does NOT occur (what predicts a model correctly reusing its result) to test the retrieval-failure account from the null side. Decisive metric: accuracy change on corrective-containing items with injection vs. withheld, plus a predictor analysis of no-recompute cases. Convincing: with the corrective-aware trigger, accuracy on corrective items drops < 1 point while blind-recompute savings are retained, and attention-to-original predicts no-recompute cases. Indecision: 1-3 point drop. Negative (> 3 point drop): blind and corrective recomputation cannot be cheaply separated, bounding H3 to easy items.

Experiment 7 (H1/H2 - Generality across data and scale): Transfer detector and onset probe across datasets and the 1.5B/7B/14B/Qwen3-8B models without retraining, with a problem-level split to avoid overfitting to GSM8K/MATH-style traces. Decisive metric: transferred onset-probe AUROC relative to in-domain, and recompute-token-fraction stability across scales. Convincing: transfer retains >= 80% of in-domain AUROC on at least three scales and prevalence stays within a factor of 2. Indecision: retention in [60%, 80%]. Negative (< 60% retention or prevalence varying by > 3x): the phenomenon is idiosyncratic across models.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Detecting semantically-equivalent recomputations is nontrivial and may be noisy; we mitigate with parsing, an LLM-judge under explicit exclusion rules, and human validation, but false positives could over-trigger. Some recomputation is beneficial (self-correction, verification), so the trigger must separate blind from corrective re-derivation, which may be hard on the hardest items. The retrieval-failure hypothesis may be wrong - recomputation might be a deliberate learned strategy - which would be an informative negative that still yields a named waste category. Memory injection alters context and could introduce distribution shift or new errors. Intervention gains may not exceed strong reactive-pruning baselines; in that case the standalone contribution is the structured diagnosis, whose adopters are reasoning-model deployers wanting cheaper inference and interpretability researchers studying working memory - a distinction we keep explicit between user-facing and research benefit. Results may be model-family specific and biphasic across scales.
